text:
lena: Hey team — started getting 401 invalid_api_key on my prod calls since yesterday. Didn't rotate keys.

lena: curl I'm running:
```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX_REDACTED_XXX\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

lena: Response is 401 with body: `{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key invalid"}`

jamie: sorry you're hitting that. quick q — did you copy the key from a mobile notes app or slack? any chance of invisible chars when copying?

lena: copied from an internal notes doc on my phone, then pasted into the env var on the server via SSH (I know, risky). I can paste the exact value here if that helps (will mask)

lena: masked paste: `sk_live_XXXREDACTED	_XXX` (looks normal)

jamie: can you run a quick hex dump on the pasted value on the server to check for non-printing codepoints? e.g.
```
# show byte values, replace KEYFILE with a file that contains the pasted key
xxd -g 1 -u KEYFILE | head -n 4
```

jamie: or run this tiny python to see codepoints:
```
python3 - <<'PY'
s = open('KEYFILE','rb').read().decode('utf-8', 'replace')
print([hex(ord(c)) for c in s])
PY
```

lena: running now...

lena: output: `["0x73", "0x6b", "0x5f", "0x6c", "0x69", "0x76", "0x65", "0x5f", "0x31", "0x32", "0x30", "0x2d", "0x200d", "0x33", "0x34"]`

jamie: there it is — `0x200d` (ZERO WIDTH JOINER) embedded between bytes. that's why the server rejects it, the key string doesn't match the server-side stored key.

rohit: interesting — we see a lot of these from mobile copy/paste. two immediate actions:
- instruct support to ask customers to check for ZWSP/ZWJ/BOM when troubleshooting
- engineering: add detection to auth validation to return a clearer error when non-printing characters are present (and emit a metric)

jamie: proposed quick repro steps for our docs / support playbook:
```
# detect invisible characters
# show unicode codepoints
python3 - <<'PY'
s = open('KEYFILE','rb').read().decode('utf-8', 'replace')
for i,c in enumerate(s):
    print(i, c, hex(ord(c)))
PY

# quick strip (workaround) - retype or sanitize in python
python3 - <<'PY'
s = open('KEYFILE').read()
clean = ''.join(c for c in s if ord(c) > 31)
open('CLEAN_KEY','w').write(clean)
print('wrote CLEAN_KEY')
PY
```

lena: re-typed the key manually into the env file and restarted, calls now succeed (200). thanks!

jamie: great. marking this as resolved for the customer. I'll add the troubleshooting snippet to the KB and link to it in the ticket.

rohit: I'll open a small PR to the auth service to:
- detect / log non-printing chars in the incoming Authorization header (no PII),
- return `invalid_api_key: contains non-printing characters` as the error string for easier troubleshooting,
- add a datadog metric `auth.invalid_key_non_printing`

rohit: ETA for PR: today, deploy to staging tomorrow.

lena: lovely, appreciate the quick help :heart:

support-bot: incident-notes saved to ticket #SUP-2241

deploy-bot: rohit pushed branch auth/zw-insert-detect -> CI queued

jamie: leaving a note to update the 'how to paste your API key' section in our onboarding docs (explicitly mention zero-width joiner/space and BOM).

jamie: resolved for now — reopen if it recurs.
